1#_: (Siman 120 seif 1) One who buys from a non-Jew. See these laws in responsum Beit Yehuda (siman 52).
2#_: (There) Coated with lead. Vessels that were immersed and afterward coated with lead require immersion again. See Magen Avraham (Orach Chaim siman 451 s.k. 27).
3#_: (There in the gloss) And so is the practice. In Keneset HaGedolah (glosses to Beit Yosef letter 18) he wrote: one should investigate our large earthenware barrels coated with lead in which we place wine — in which mikveh can one immerse them, for certainly the mikveh water cannot contain them because of their size; and I found in responsum of Keneset Yisrael to the sage Mahari Za'avi that there is no remedy except through artifice — to give them to a non-Jew as a gift and borrow them back; and the sage Mahari Milada wrote on this that it appears to him that immersion is not required, for only eating vessels require immersion, and these barrels are only for placing wine for preservation; and his teacher agreed with him. But in Ohr U'Me'ir I found that large metal vessels in which wine is stored require immersion; and perhaps one may say that Ohr U'Me'ir meant only metal vessels, for everyone requires immersion, but for earthenware coated with lead, where there is dispute whether immersion is required — for these large barrels one may rely on this to store wine without immersion; and accordingly, those coated with lead inside and outside, which are like pure metal, require immersion — end of his words.
4#_: (Shach s.k. 4) He immerses without a blessing. And if coated inside and outside, it requires a blessing — Peri Chadash. Nevertheless one may say that specifically coated with actual lead, but glazed earthenware — one does not bless; see Mishbetzot Zahav (Orach Chaim siman 451 s.k. 131).
5#_: (Seif 3) He blesses on immersion of a vessel. If he did not bless before immersion — requires study whether he can bless afterward; see Eshel Avraham (Orach Chaim siman 323 s.k. 13).
6#_: (Seif 7 in the gloss) And likewise a pepper mill. And a coffee mill — according to Taz (s.k. 4) one immerses without a blessing, since coffee requires cooking; according to Shach (s.k. 11) one may say it does not require immersion, for it is not fit for anything else.
7#_: (Taz s.k. 16) D'oraisa. Accordingly it appears to me that for glass vessels we believe a minor, for in any case according to everyone immersion is only d'rabbanan, as Peri Chadash wrote (this siman s.k. 3 and s.k. 26); likewise Sha'agat Aryeh and likewise responsum Pri Megadim (part 2 siman 96). However, according to what Tosafot Eruvin (daf 41) wrote — that specifically regarding their own matter that rests upon them minors are believed in d'rabbanan matters, but not for agency — see there. If so, here when one sends a minor to immerse glass vessels, one may say no; and see Minchat Chinuch (siman 337 seif 8 katan) and what he wrote in the gloss there.
